items.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: he called me and asked me if I would be interested in it

ctx.x: Okay. Your work, composing work, in addition to “Quiet Now” of course, has appeared in some interesting places, including “Sesame Street” and “The Invasion of the Body Snatchers.” How did that film come about?

The film opportunity came about through a back door, sort of analogous to the John Hammond story. It turns out that Phillip Kaufman, the director who made “Invasion of the Body Snatchers,” was from Chicago and had heard me play years earlier, liked my playing, and had it in his head someday he wanted me to do a jazz score for one of his movies. So when “Invasion of the Body Snatchers” was just in the formative stages on the screenplay board, he called me and asked me if I would be interested in it, and at that…
